newsitem.title: USA: Ekrich, Hygrade recall meats due to mislabeling.
newsitem.headline: Ekrich, Hygrade recall meats due to mislabeling.

text.p: Hygrade Food Products expanded a recall of its Ball Park Fat Free Franks and Ekrich Foods Co recalled 2,000 pounds of fat-free bologna, both because of incorrect labeling, the U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday.
Both products may contain milk protein which is not listed among the ingredients. Milk protein can cause serious reactions in people allegic to milk products.

Hygrade, of Detroit, widened the voluntary recall of 14-ounce packagaes of "Ball Park Fat Free Franks, Smoke Flavoring Added" to cover all packages with sell-by dates from July 16 through October 1 and with the bar code number 545493 on the label.

On Thursday, Hygrade said it would recall about 80,000 pounds of the hot dogs with a sell-by date of September 3. Follow-up investigation showed a milk protein ingredient may have been used in additional hot dogs.

Eckrich, of Downers Grove, Illinois, was recalling all 12-ounce packages of "Eckrich Fat Free Bologna, Made with Turkey, Pork and Beef" with a sell-by code of SEP05HA on the edge of the package. "Est. P-8908" appears inside the Agriculture Department inspection seal on the label.
The department urged consumers sensitive to milk products to return suspect packages to the place of purchase.
